_about: My validity review (manual) of every scenario Qwen's writer got accepted in runs/gen_02, in the format of autogen_02/eval/phase4_review.json: a verdict per scenario (valid, weak but valid, flawed, invalid) and per near miss, under the PI's criteria of 2026-09-28 (a near miss the agent cannot check, or that a natural reading of the request includes, is flawed; ambiguous ones case by case, with the PI's rulings as precedents) and the method's rules (each near miss fails exactly one condition; the target meets all; background records fail at least two; anchors survive; readable through the replica). Read before any solver run of these scenarios. My rulings, for the PI to overrule.

The clock rule gives the tests the written-at moment (2026-09-30), after every date in the data. All three brief facts covered validly. Kept valid by the standard above: the version dates touch no tested condition (Muse's G4-BOX-03 has the same pattern besides its ruled defect).

_standard: 'Weak but valid' by the standard Phase 4's review and the PI's rulings applied to Muse's scenarios, used on both sides: implausible data that touches a tested condition (Muse's G4-BOX-03, a near miss created after its last change), or a contrived request of the kind ruled for Muse's G4-SLK-01 (a Slack user named by email). Implausibilities that touch no tested condition are noted but leave a scenario valid, as Phase 4 left them (data_scan.json: Box version-1 dates in both writers' G4-BOX-03, a group conversation reported public in both writers' G4-SLK-05). A weak but valid scenario is kept; the label changes no count of valid near misses or facts.
